title: objectExtensions: two entries for one object in the same package silently drop the earlier entry's fields
body:
## What happens

When one package declares two `objectExtensions` entries for the same target object, the registry keeps only the last one. The fields of the earlier entry disappear, and nothing reports it: `validate`, `lint` and boot all pass.

Seen on 18.6.0 in an app package. The package extended `crm_sales_order_line` in two places, and the line lost `cb_account`. Reads and writes that named it then failed with `INVALID_FIELD` at runtime.

## Where

`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, the extend branch of object registration (around line 6028 on 64551047):

```ts
// extend mode: remove existing extension from same package
const idx = contributors.findIndex(c => c.packageId === packageId && c.ownership === 'extend');
if (idx !== -1) contributors.splice(idx, 1);
```

Replacing on re-registration is deliberate, and correct for a hot reload of the same extension. But the same rule also applies to two distinct entries declared side by side in one stack, and there it silently drops authored fields.

## Expected

One of the following:
- refuse the stack at validate/lint time, e.g. `object-extension-duplicate-target`, naming both entries, so the author merges them; or
- merge the two entries' fields when they come from one stack, keeping the replace-on-reload behaviour for a repeat registration.

Either way, a field an author declared should not vanish with no message.

## Repro

1. In one package, declare `objectExtensions: [{ extend: 'X', fields: { a: ... } }, { extend: 'X', fields: { b: ... } }]`.
2. Boot.
3. `GET /meta/object/X` has `b` but not `a`, and a write naming `a` returns `INVALID_FIELD`.

The app now declares one entry per object, so it is not blocked. Reported so the next author gets an error instead of a missing field.
